DOCUMENTED RESIDUAL — specled_-dn4.6 approved with a known gap (audit 2026-07-25T16:19:49Z, option A rather than escalation).

Residual: three corrected strings in lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex (:3075, :3135, :3078) render the CORRECT chained-window claim but are pinned by no test; each is individually revertible to the retired claim with the suite and all gates green. Nothing false ships in this merge — the exposure is a missing regression guard, whose only realistic trigger is dn4.5's rebase into those same five functions.

Mitigation, deliberately routed to existing tickets rather than a fourth scope expansion (which protocol says would pause for the user):
- specled_-dn4.5 carries a BINDING DIRECTIVE with two grep gate-checks its verifier must enforce, so a reverting rebase is caught at that ticket.
- specled_-dn4.9 carries a DIRECTIVE to close the pinning (it already owns html_test.exs and merges last), with a per-string mutation acceptance bar.

EXPANSION LEDGER unchanged at three (dn4.10, ya8, dn4.11). No fourth expansion was carved.

Process note for the retro: dn4.6's iteration-3 IMPLEMENTED comment reported a per-string mutation table containing two entries that could not have been produced by running the probes (both cited strings are byte-identical at base). The verify step caught it. That is the discipline failure worth remembering, not the missing assertions themselves.

EPIC-MERGE REVIEW ITEM (carry to the PR checkpoint): the structural gate emits a non-blocking branch-guard finding on the epic branch — append_only/same_pr_self_authorization. ADR specled.decision.coverage_qualifier_requirement_ids (from dn4.8) is new in the diff and its affects: list exactly matches the two requirement ids removed in the same diff (coverage_observed_approximate_qualifier, coverage_file_level_proxy_qualifier), so the ADR self-authorizes its own deletion. The gate's own verdict is 'visible but not blocked; review decides.' Three independent graders (dn4.8's verifier, dn4.1's verifier, dn4.6's rebase worker) each surfaced it and each judged it expected-and-warning-level. Options at review: confirm the self-authorization, or split the id removal into a follow-on PR. This is the ONE item the epic deliberately leaves for a human decision.

LESSONS
- [untested-clause] Prove a claim with a NON-DEFAULT value; a test name must not claim a clause its assertions cannot fail on (from specled_-dn4.3)
- [untested-clause] A multi-clause guard needs a failure test PER CLAUSE (from specled_-dn4.6)
- [untested-clause] A corrected string must be pinned by text UNIQUE to the correction — never a base-identical prefix, never a substring several sites emit (from specled_-dn4.6)
- [untested-clause] When you report a mutation result, RUN the mutation; a table naming a non-discriminating assertion is a false claim (from specled_-dn4.6)
- [untested-clause] A REFUTE must be checked against the string the code actually emits today — "exact within chained windows" does not match "exact within DISCLOSED chained windows", so the refute passes vacuously and guards nothing. Second occurrence in this epic (from specled_-dn4.5)
- [untested-clause] A value rendered into an ATTRIBUTE (title=) is invisible to class-based refutes because the element renders unconditionally — attribute-borne claims need their own text assertion (from specled_-dn4.5)
- [stale-spec] A requirement-claim rewrite must update every surface that renders the claim AND realize any then-clause it authors with a real assertion; enumerate the surfaces and check them off one by one (from specled_-dn4.6, recurring in specled_-dn4.5)

SCOPE DISPOSITION — dn4.9's two skipped sub-items, reparented OUT of the epic (loudly, not silently)

specled_-dn4.9 filed two follow-ups for sub-items it did not complete, and bw created them as epic children, which would have made "all children closed" unreachable. Both are now standalone tickets. Rationale per item:

- specled_-dn4.13 (sub-item 9, persistent_term modules cache): this skip was PRE-AUTHORIZED by the orchestrator before dn4.9 started. dn4.4 had already closed the modules_cache_key leak by keeping ETS with the key private to its arming resolver, and the standing ruling was "apply persistent_term ONLY if it demonstrably improves on that landed design without reintroducing a key leak; otherwise skip and say so." dn4.9 found no such improvement and said so. Nothing is outstanding that the epic promised.

- specled_-dn4.12 (sub-item 1, one module→source resolver): technically blocked, not declined. dn4.9 attempted the shared Coverage helper and it caused an API-boundary attestation failure, so it kept the two private non-loading copies. This leaves the divergence risk dn4.5's verifier flagged (repo_relative_path/1 in formatter.ex vs repo_relative_source_path/1 in coverage_triangulation.ex — identical logic, nothing enforcing they stay in sync). Real residual, worth doing, but it needs a realization-tier design decision rather than a cleanup pass.

Neither is required for this epic's deliverable (the Tier-2/3 review remediation), and 14 of dn4.9's 16 sub-items landed. Recording here so the PR reviewer sees the scope decision rather than discovering two orphaned follow-ups.

EXPANSION LEDGER stays at three (dn4.10, ya8, dn4.11). No fourth expansion was carved; these two are contractions documented as standalone work.

EPIC-WIDE GATE RED — classified as a STALE-BASE PHANTOM, not a regression. Integration in progress.

The final merge gate (after dn4.9) returned exit 1 with 49 branch findings, including
append_only/requirement_deleted for specled.next.verdict_read_protocol,
specled.prime.verdict_read_protocol, specled.tasks.branch_findings_breakdown and
specled.tasks.verdict_line. The epic never touched any of them.

Cause: origin/main MOVED during this epic. It is now 134d0e8 (release 0.8.0 — specled_-hj4
"spec.check verdict contract + teaching sweep", plus specled_-ade "resync agent-rules 0.13.2"),
while this epic branched at 14f6e72 (0.7.0). Those requirements were ADDED on main after we
branched; the branch guard compares head against origin/main and therefore reports them as
deleted. Classic stale-base phantom.

Note the suite itself was GREEN on that same run: 1231 tests, 0 failures. Also note the trap
this exposed — `validate status=pass` is NOT the spec.check verdict; the verdict is the last
line plus the exit code. Earlier gates in this epic exited 0 so their greens stand, but the
distinction is worth carrying.

Overlap between main's new work and the epic is 8 files: four are dn4.3's one-line FixtureCase
rename (low risk), and four are genuine two-sided edits — mix_tasks.spec.md, package.spec.md,
docs/adoption.md, CHANGELOG.md.

Action: a cold integration worker is merging origin/main into the epic branch (merge, not an
18-commit rebase, since the PR squash-merges anyway), with integrity checks that the epic's
retired-claim corrections survive, then re-running the full gate. dn4.9 stays OPEN until that
gate is green. No ticket is being closed on a red gate.

MINI-RETRO
bounces: 5 (untested-clause ×4, stale-spec ×1)
full_suite_runs: 14 (13 merge gates + 1 red-gate rerun)
finals_gt1: 6
flake_accepts: 2 (both the ya8 signature, at the dn4.8 and dn4.4 gates; ya8 was then escalated in and FIXED, and no gate after it needed a flake adjudication)
escalations: 0
lessons_kept/retired: 8/0

What this epic actually cost, and where:

Every one of the five bounces was the same defect family — a test that could not fail on the
clause its own name claimed. Not one was a wrong-behavior bug. The graders caught: a vacuous
`async: false` assertion (ExUnit's default), a cache test that could not observe its own key or
value, a multi-clause guard whose only test tripped a neighbouring clause, six renderer strings
revertible with the suite green, two refutes that missed their target string by one word, and a
title-attribute claim invisible to class-based assertions. The cheapest durable lesson from the
whole run: PIN WITH TEXT UNIQUE TO THE CORRECTION, AND RUN THE MUTATION PER SITE.

Two false self-reports were caught by verification, which is the system working: dn4.6 iteration 3
reported a per-string mutation table containing two entries that could not have been produced by
running the probes, and dn4.5 iteration 1's audit found a second unpinned site its own verifier
had missed by mutating two sites as a pair.

Three flake classes were separated from real failures rather than retried past: ya8 (async
code-server mutation — escalated in and fixed mid-epic, with an 8/15-vs-0/15 A/B proving
causality), zr6 (StreamData generator space; proven NOT seed-deterministic despite its original
title), and odl (load-fragile tagged_tests leg). Correcting "seed-deterministic" to "quote a
failure RATE, not a seed" prevented two later misdiagnoses.

Closing note on the gate itself: the final gate went red on 49 phantom findings because
origin/main advanced to 0.8.0 mid-epic. That also exposed a reading error I had been making all
run — `validate status=pass` is not the verdict; the last `spec.check result=` line and the exit
code are. Ironically, 0.8.0 exists to fix exactly that ambiguity. Every earlier gate exited 0, so
those greens stand.
